title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. The page belongs to a sequence of elementary lemmas about binomial coefficients c_{ij} = C(i+j, i), the structure constants of the divided-power polynomial algebra S = k<T>, where T^{(i)}T^{(j)} = c_{ij} T^{(i+j)}. The aim, completed on the next page, is to show that a k-module M can be recovered from the graded S-module of 'tails' sum_{i>=N} M·T^{(i)}, i.e. that M -> omega_N(M) is fully faithful. This is a technical step toward the divided-power de Rham complex, the subject of the 1976 IHES lecture.

(1) End of the proof of Lemma 2.
Set-up from the previous page. Fix p and N, and choose e with p^e >= N+1. Put y_eps = x_{N+p^eps} - x_N for 0 <= eps <= e. Grothendieck works with the weak system S-bar(N, e, y):
- y_eps = 0 whenever C(N+p^eps, N) is nonzero mod p;
- y_eps = y_0 whenever C(N+p^eps, N+1) is nonzero mod p, for eps >= 1.
The claim is that S-bar(N, e, y) implies y_0 = 0. The proof is by induction on N.
- If p does not divide N+1, then C(N+1, N) = N+1 is a unit and y_0 = 0 at once.
- Otherwise write N+1 = (N'+1)p. By Lucas' theorem, for eps >= 1:
  - C(N+p^eps, N) ≡ C(N'+p^{eps-1}, N') mod p;
  - C(N+p^eps, N+1) ≡ C(N'+p^{eps-1}, N'+1) mod p.
  So, with e' = e-1 and y'_eps = y_{eps+1}, the system becomes S-bar(N', e', y').
  - The second equation at eps = 0 has coefficient C(N'+1, N'+1) = 1, so it gives y'_0 = y_0.
  - The hypothesis is preserved: p^e >= N+1 = (N'+1)p gives p^{e'} >= N'+1.
  - Since N' < N, induction gives y'_0 = 0, hence y_0 = 0 ('cqfd. Ouf!').

(2) Theorem 1.
Statement. Let E be an abelian group and (x_i) a family with C(j, i)(x_j - x_i) = 0 for all j > i >= N. Then x_i = x_N for all i >= N.
Proof.
- An element of E vanishes iff it vanishes in every localization E_(p), so we may assume E is a Z_(p)-module.
- Binomial coefficients prime to p are then units, so the hypotheses restricted to the indices N, N+1, N+p^eps imply the weak system.
- Lemma 2 gives x_{N+1} = x_N.
- Induction on N (the hypothesis for N implies it for N+1) gives the rest.

(3) Corollary 1 (set-up only on this page).
- S = k<T> and S^{+(N)} = sum_{i>=N} k·T^{(i)}, a divided-power ideal.
- For a k-module M, omega_N(M) = M ⊗ S^{+(N)} = sum_{i>=N} M·T^{(i)}, a graded S-module.
- Next page: (a) omega_N is fully faithful; (b) M is identified with the compatible systems (x_i)_{i>=N} in prod M·T^{(i)} satisfying T^{(j)} x_i = c_{ij} x_{i+j}. Via x_i = xi_i T^{(i)}, (b) reduces exactly to Theorem 1.
errors: omega_N(M) is written M ⊗_S S^{+(N)}; for a k-module M it should be M ⊗_k S^{+(N)} (= sum_{i>=N} M·T^{(i)}), as the right-hand side indicates. Slip of notation.
The system is written S-bar'(N', 0', ...); it should be S-bar(N', e', (y'_eps)), the same system with N, e replaced by N', e'. Notational slip only.
Minor: the reduction to x_{N+1} = x_N by 'récurrence' tacitly uses that the hypothesis for N implies it for N+1. True, but unstated.
No mathematical error: the Lucas-theorem reduction and the induction check out.

ideas.what: Elementary lemma: if C(j,i)(x_j - x_i) = 0 for all j > i >= N in an abelian group, then the x_i are constant for i >= N. Proved via localization at p and Lucas' theorem by descent N -> (N+1)/p - 1.
ideas.modern_name: p-adic properties of binomial coefficients (Lucas/Kummer theorems); gcd-type statements on binomial coefficients
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lucas (1878), Kummer (1852) for the underlying facts; this specific lemma is folklore-level

ideas.what: Full faithfulness of M -> omega_N(M) = M ⊗ S^{+(N)} into graded modules over the divided-power polynomial algebra k<T>; M is recovered from any 'tail' of the divided-power grading.
ideas.modern_name: Graded modules over the divided-power algebra Γ_k(T); truncations of the PD filtration
ideas.usually_credited_to: Background in Berthelot's crystalline cohomology (1974) and Berthelot–Ogus; this specific statement is not standardly attributed

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but elementary combinatorial lemma on binomial coefficients, serving a routine full-faithfulness statement for divided-power graded modules. It is correct and nicely done, but contains nothing a specialist would find new or significant.
transcription_corrections: 'S-bar'(N', 0', (y'_eps))' should read 'S-bar(N', e', (y'_eps)_{0<=eps<=e'})' (as in the manuscript's intent).
'OPS E un module sur un Z_p' should read 'OPS E un module sur Z_(p)' (localized integers), i.e. 'module sur Z_(p)'.
'on retiendra que les x_i' should be 'on ne retiendra que les x_i' (only the x_i with i = N or N+p^eps are used).
In Cor 1: 'pour un k-module M' (an 'M' is crossed out); '⊗_S' in omega_N(M) is as written but should mathematically be '⊗_k'.
